correctness.rationale: All nine morphisms are exhausted by 2 choices of zero-leading binary images with one 1 and 3 choices for its mate, plus 1 choice zero-leading two-1 image and 3 mates. For six nonconstant fixed points, all four ordered boundary-letter pairs occur at every separation d>=3: finite witnesses for d=3..8 within sigma^8(0), followed by strong induction using the exact 3k+s offset recurrence and 18 surjective pair-map identities. For each length 3k+r and starting block offset, the count is kc plus a two-boundary-letter correction; attained minima/maxima from the full-lag lemma give the six-by-three exact envelopes, and sliding one position changes count by <=1 so all intervening counts occur. The length 1..8 boundary is independently checked, and equal-image cases are period-three. Independent prefix enumeration verified all 9 morphisms for n=1..128 (1152 cases) and independently checked the 54 full-lag base/map cases. The induction, not finite tests, establishes every n.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge complete natural nine-morphism classification. Rigo–Stipulanti–Whiteland 2024 prove general automaticity for Parikh-collinear fixed points; their concluding section explicitly asks whether the much more restrictive Parikh-constant class has ultimately periodic abelian complexity. Automaticity does not imply ultimate periodicity; full trichotomy in smallest nontrivial odd uniform binary class is not an immediate corollary, despite elementary constant-image special cases.

final_claim: Exact abelian-complexity trichotomy for all nine full-support binary length-three Parikh-constant substitutions prolongable on 0. Equal-image cases have a(n)=1 if 3|n else 2; four specified nonconstant pairs have a(n)=3 if 3|n else 2; remaining two pairs have a(1)=2 and a(n)=3 for n>=2.
